verdict.rationale: HumanLayer documents running its remote daemon on your own hosts: a cloud VM, workstation, or private-network machine. Its site also claims you can run the HumanLayer stack on your workstation or remote workers, which covers the local and own-VM parts of the story. However, tasks are controlled from the hosted app.humanlayer.com, so the evidence shows self-hosted execution workers rather than fully self-hosted infrastructure, and containers are never mentioned. missing for 10: documented container/Docker deployment, evidence that the control plane itself can be self-hosted, independent or hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can self-host agent infrastructure locally, in containers, or on my own VMs

citations.quote: The host can be a cloud VM, workstation, or private-network machine.
run the HumanLayer stack on your workstation or remote workers
This guide shows you how to install, authenticate, and launch a remote daemon.
You will control the task from app.humanlayer.com on a machine or phone.
